treaty_name: Agreement between the United Kingdom and Qatar for the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income and on capital gains (2009, as amended 2010)
eif_quote: SIGNED 25 JUNE 2009 AMENDING PROTOCOL SIGNED 20 OCTOBER 2010 (Consolidated version) Entered into force 15 October 2010 and 27 July 2011 respectively Effective from 1 January 2004 for profits, income and gains from shipping and air transport, from 1 January 2011 for taxes withheld at source, and for other taxes, in respect of taxable or financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2011.
source_title: 2009 UK-Qatar Double Taxation Agreement, as amended by 2010 protocol (HMRC consolidated version) and MLI synthesised text (gov.uk)

rates.quote: (2) However, such dividends may also be taxed in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the dividends is a resident of the other Contracting State; (a) except as provided in sub-paragraph 2 (b) such dividends shall be exempt from tax in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident;

However, such royalties may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the royalties is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 5 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.quote: Notwithstanding any provisions of [this Agreement], a benefit under [this Agreement] shall not be granted in respect of an item of income or capital if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of [this Agreement].

notes: Dividends: exempt at source, except (other than for pension schemes) dividends paid out of income from immovable property by a tax-exempt property investment vehicle distributing most of its income annually (e.g. REIT), capped at 15% (Art. 10(2)(b)) — not modelled as a tier. INTEREST omitted: Art. 11(2) gives no general source-State cap; interest is taxable only in the residence State only if a condition of Art. 11(3) is met — beneficial owner is the State/political subdivision/statutory body, an individual, a listed company, a company less than 25% owned by non-residents of its State, a pension scheme, or an unrelated financial institution (not back-to-back), or the interest is paid by a State, by a bank in the ordinary course of banking business, or on a quoted Eurobond; otherwise no treaty limit. MLI Art. 7(1) PPT replaced the main-purpose clauses in Arts. 10(6), 11(7), 12(7); effective for WHT from 1 January 2021 per gov.uk. No MLI Art. 8 holding-period clause appears in the synthesised text. Effective for WHT from 1 January 2011 (Art. 26(2)(a) and HMRC consolidated note).
